cards.text: Ezekiel, a prophet, is telling us about his vision of a temple. A man has been leading him all through it, and now the man brings Ezekiel back to the temple entrance. Ezekiel looks down at the threshold and sees something coming out from under it, heading east.

cards.question: Ezekiel is standing at the temple entrance. What's coming out from under the threshold?

cards.text: Water, coming down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar. Then the man leads Ezekiel out the north gate and around the outside to the outer gate facing east.

cards.question: True or false: Out at the east gate, the water coming from the temple is already a big rushing stream.

cards.text: Nope. It's a trickle, like when you turn on the garden hose and it just kind of… SIGHS at you.
Then the man heads east with a measuring line in his hand. He measures off a thousand cubits and leads Ezekiel right through the water.

cards.question: The water started as a trickle at the temple. After the man's first thousand cubits, how deep is it?
The man measures another thousand cubits, and the water is at Ezekiel's knees. He measures one more thousand, and now it's up to Ezekiel's ___.
True or false: After the man measures one more thousand cubits, Ezekiel can still cross the water on foot.

cards.text: No way, it's a river deep enough for swimming now. Speaking as a stamper on a gold base, I don't swim, friend. I SINK.
Then the man asks Ezekiel, "Son of man, do you see this?" and leads him back to the bank of the river.

cards.question: Back on the bank, what does Ezekiel see along both sides of the river?

cards.text: Then the man tells Ezekiel this water flows east, down into the Arabah, and empties into the Dead Sea. The DEAD Sea, friend, that's like naming your bakery Burnt.

cards.question: When the river from the temple empties into the Dead Sea, what happens to the water there?
The man says swarms of living creatures and a great number of fish will show up wherever the ___ flows.

cards.text: Fishermen will stand on the shore from En-gedi to En-eglaim, spreading their nets. Fishing at the Dead Sea is like my old junk drawer getting a WAITING LIST.

cards.question: The fishermen spread their nets along the shore. What do they pull in?
True or false: Where the river reaches the Dead Sea, the swamps and marshes become fresh too.

cards.text: Not those. The man says the swamps and marshes will be left for salt.
Now back to those trees on the riverbanks. The man says fruit trees of all kinds will grow along both sides of the river.

cards.question: True or false: Someday the leaves on the fruit trees by the river will wither and their fruit will run out.
The fruit trees along the river bear fruit every single ___.
Why do the fruit trees along the river keep producing like that?

answers.text: The water from the sanctuary flows to them
The fishermen carry water up to them
The rain falls on them all year long

cards.question: The fruit from the trees by the river is for food. What are their leaves for?

cards.text: Fruit EVERY month, and I've had ovens that couldn't promise me Tuesday. Hang on, friend, because Ezekiel's vision isn't over yet.

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage: that Ezekiel is seeing a vision of a temple and that a man has been leading him all through it (Ezekiel 40:2-3). The card cites only Ezekiel 47:1 and gives no reference for these facts.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card may have 3. Every other story card is limited to 1 or 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 3 already says the river brings 'a great number of fish.' That rules out the wrong answer 'Only a few small fish' before the baker reaches this question.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The cards before this one say life comes wherever the river flows. That setup leads a thoughtful baker to answer True. The exception in verse 11 ('But the swamps and marshes...') can't be reasoned out from what the baker has seen, so the setup points the baker away from the right answer.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: 'Now back to those trees on the riverbanks' says the trees Ezekiel sees in verse 7 are the fruit trees the man says will grow in verse 12. The text never makes that connection.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
